sources.title: Afghanistan Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: Live U.S. Department of State guidance gives U.S.-passport entry information and identifies current Afghan visa-recognition uncertainty.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Afghan immigration officials may refuse to accept visas that were issued by Afghan Republic-era officials.

sources.title: Burkina Faso Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: Live U.S. Department of State guidance expressly reports Burkina Faso's nationality-specific visa-issuance suspension.
sources.supportingExcerpt: As of Dec 30, 2025, the Government of Burkina Faso suspended visas to Americans with limited exceptions.

sources.title: Chad Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: Live U.S. Department of State guidance addresses visa issuance and arrival issuance for U.S. citizens.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Government of Chad is not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens at this time.

sources.title: Iran Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: Live U.S. Department of State guidance states the U.S.-visitor tourist-visa liability but no usable issuance route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A tourist visa is required, except for Kish Island.

sources.title: North Korea Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: Live U.S. Department of State guidance establishes the special-validation restriction on ordinary U.S. passports.
sources.supportingExcerpt: U.S. passports are not valid for travel into or through North Korea unless they contain a special validation.

sources.title: Mali Travel Advisory
sources.officialityEvidence: Live U.S. Department of State guidance expressly reports Mali's nationality-specific visa-issuance suspension.
sources.supportingExcerpt: As of January 1, 2026, the government of Mali suspended visa issuance to U.S. citizens.

sources.title: Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza International Travel Information
sources.jurisdiction: United States / Israel, West Bank and Gaza
sources.officialityEvidence: Live U.S. Department of State entry guidance distinguishes governing authorities and crossing-specific controls for the West Bank and Gaza.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All persons seeking to enter or depart Israel, the West Bank, or Gaza are subject to immigration and security screening.

conflicts.explanation: Current State Department guidance says Burkina Faso suspended visas to Americans from 30 December 2025, with limited exceptions. This cannot be represented as a functioning ordinary visitor eVisa route.

conflicts.officialStatus: unavailable (not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens)
conflicts.explanation: Current State Department guidance says Chad is not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens and visas are unavailable on arrival. The fallback advance-visa label does not describe current ordinary issuance.
Current State Department guidance says Mali suspended visa issuance to U.S. citizens from 1 January 2026, with limited exceptions. This cannot be represented as a functioning ordinary visitor route.

unresolved.reason: The State Department says an Afghan visa is required before travel but warns that Afghanistan may refuse some overseas-mission visas. It does not establish a current usable ordinary-passport issuance channel.
Current guidance reports a suspension of visas to Americans with limited exceptions. That exceptional suspension cannot be normalized as a functioning ordinary short-visitor route.
Current guidance says Chad is not routinely issuing visas to U.S. citizens. It therefore does not establish a reliable ordinary visitor issuance route or timing.
Current guidance states tourist-visa liability but does not establish an ordinary U.S.-passport issuance mode or usable nationwide visitor route. No portal route is inferred.

An ordinary U.S. passport is invalid for North Korea travel without narrowly granted special validation. No ordinary visitor issuance route is established, and the taxonomy has no passport-invalid status.
Current guidance reports a suspension of visa issuance to U.S. citizens with limited exceptions. That exceptional suspension cannot be normalized as a functioning ordinary short-visitor route.

Current guidance distinguishes Israeli, Palestinian and Egyptian crossing controls, security screening, and Gaza access. It does not establish one ordinary U.S.-passport status for the PS destination scope.
